name: Inverse IFEval
intro: 大型语言模型（LLMs）在处理与训练范式冲突的指令时表现出认知惯性。Inverse IFEval基准旨在评估LLMs克服训练偏见并遵循对抗性指令的能力。该基准包含八种挑战类型，涵盖23个领域，通过人机协作流程构建了1012个高质量的中英文问题，并采用LLM-as-a-Judge框架进行评估。
org: ByteDance Seed, Nanjing University, Peking University, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunica
intro_en: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit cognitive inertia when handling instructions that conflict with their training paradigms. The Inverse IFEval benchmark aims to assess LLMs' ability to overcome training biases and follow adversarial instructions. It includes eight challenge types across 23 domains, featuring 1,012 high-quality Chinese and English questions created through a human-AI collaborative process, and is evaluated using the LLM-as-a-Judge framework.

drawio_review_note:
Aligned with arXiv:2509.04292. Inverse IFEval builds a 1,012-question bilingual benchmark through five stages: observation and reversal, seed data construction, large-scale generation, automatic filtering, and human verification. The authors analyze common SFT response paradigms and invert them into eight counterintuitive instruction types. LLM training experts craft seed questions for each type, with cross-functional review requiring unanimous qualified/unqualified decisions. Prompt templates and a disciplinary taxonomy guide multiple strong LLMs to generate candidates, initially 20 per domain-type combination. Automatic filters apply length constraints and semantic similarity checks, with targeted generation for underrepresented domains and cross-model verification. Experts review type consistency, instruction clarity, and rubrics. The final Chinese/English dataset includes metadata and standardized rubrics and is evaluated with optimized LLM-as-a-Judge templates, model selection, and prompts validated against human scores.

Bilingual Draw.io bundle synchronized from benchmark_importer after paper and official-source review. The Chinese and English specs use identical node IDs, semantic types, coordinates, edges, and waypoints; strict Draw.io validation, XML and link checks, and rendered-image visual review passed before publication.
